raw_plan.interpretation: I interpret this as a single acquisition email introducing Tally to a prospective SaaS/startup product team, with creating a free form as the one next step. It is not onboarding because no existing product use is established.
raw_plan.reader: A SaaS or startup product team evaluating a way to collect structured feedback from users without introducing per-form or per-submission charges within ordinary fair-use boundaries.
raw_plan.reader_segment: SaaS/startup product teams building feedback loops
raw_plan.reader_scope: Write at the selected audience level. Do not assume the recipient currently uses Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets, Make, webhooks, or any particular form builder.
raw_plan.promise: Tally gives product teams a form they can place on a product page and use to collect feedback, with unlimited forms and submissions free within its fair usage guidelines.
raw_plan.orientation: Tally is an online form builder for collecting product feedback on your own pages and routing submissions into the tools your team uses.
raw_plan.arc: In this one-email arc, introduce the product through one immediately useful operation, make the free offer concrete, qualify it honestly, and invite the reader to create their first form.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A single acquisition email needs one broadly relevant reason to try Tally, not a catalogue of integrations. The embed mechanism makes the product tangible for a product team, while the free unlimited-forms-and-submissions offer lowers the barrier to taking the requested next step. The narrower Airtable proposition is retained as a complete alternative because it is especially relevant to the researched subsegment, but it should not become the primary premise for recipients whose stack is unknown. The single thing that would most change this campaign: can the source at https://tally.so/ be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

Put a feedback form directly on your product page, so customers can submit their thoughts without leaving the page.

Tally is an online form builder for creating that feedback form. Add the Tally widget script and an iframe with data-tally-src to your site, and the form renders inline.

You can create unlimited forms and collect unlimited submissions for free, as long as your use stays within Tally’s fair usage guidelines.

events.body:
Ask one focused product question at the point where someone is using the feature it concerns. They can respond there, without being sent to a separate form page.

Tally is an online form builder that lets you create the form first, then render it inline on your website. To embed it, add Tally’s widget script and an iframe with `data-tally-src` to the page.

Start with one question on one relevant page. It is a practical way to see how Tally fits your product-feedback loop before deciding where else a form would be useful.

You can create **unlimited forms and submissions free** while your use stays within Tally’s fair usage guidelines.

The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (inferred; applicability must be checked): Teams that embed Tally forms report wiring form submissions through either a native integration or a Make.com webhook workflow into Airtable, i.e. the audience is already attempting the Tally-to-database routing step described in the candidate's situation hypothesis.
Source: https://www.indiehackers.com/post/sync-form-responses-to-airtable-05c602efbd; quote: We just released our Airtable integration for Tally.
Source: https://community.make.com/t/help-with-sending-tally-form-submissions-to-airtable-without-6-branches/84370/2; quote: I think your challenge here is that you are using the general Webhook Module instead of the Tally App
Problem context: When syncing Tally form submissions to Airtable via a generic webhook (rather than a purpose-built app integration), some builders need many conditional branches to handle the mapping, which they experience as unwieldy. [Source limits: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://community.make.com/t/help-with-sending-tally-form-submissions-to-airtable-without-6-branches/84370/2
readers.what_it_sells: Tally offers an online form builder I could use to place a focused feedback question directly inside a product page, letting me test an in-context feedback loop without sending users elsewhere.
readers.biggest_doubt: My main reservation is product fit: the email tells me how the form is embedded but not whether it can visually fit our interface or what the embedded experience actually looks like. That uncertainty is small enough that I would still inspect the free option.
fixes: Rewrite "Ask one focused product question at the point where someone is using the feature it concerns." to include a concrete example, such as asking for feedback immediately beneath a newly used feature.

After "To embed it, add Tally’s widget script and an iframe with `data-tally-src` to the page.", add a screenshot or a factual sentence explaining what control, if any, I have over the embedded form’s appearance.

Trim "Start with one question on one relevant page. It is a practical way to see how Tally fits your product-feedback loop before deciding where else a form would be useful." to "Test one question on one product page before expanding it elsewhere."
